title: Distinguishing stone from timber without textures
summary: Stone and wood separate by roughness, edge wear and color variance, not by detail maps.
applies_when: village, architecture or prop scenes viewed closer than 15 metres

values.timber_grain_scale: grain direction follows the longest axis of each member
values.edge_wear: lighter roughness on exposed corners only, not on the whole surface

checks: at inspection distance the two materials differ in highlight shape, not only in color
no repeated identical face pattern on adjacent stones
timber grain direction contradicts no structural member
edges are worn, faces are not uniformly noisy
limits: no claim about real stone types or species
vertex-color variance needs enough mesh density; coarse meshes need per-face assignment
